name: 15b embedding lookup
title: A one-hot vector times the embedding table selects one row
subtitle: Vocabulary of 5 tokens with ids 0 to 4; embedding width 3; token "cat" has id 1

steps.caption: The token "cat" has id 1. Its one-hot vector has a 1 in position 1 and 0 everywhere else. The embedding table has one row of 3 learned numbers per token.
Column 1 of the product multiplies each one-hot entry by the matching table entry and adds them. Four of the five products are zero, so the sum is just the "cat" entry, +0.7.
Column 2 of the product multiplies each one-hot entry by the matching table entry and adds them. Four of the five products are zero, so the sum is just the "cat" entry, -0.4.
Column 3 of the product multiplies each one-hot entry by the matching table entry and adds them. Four of the five products are zero, so the sum is just the "cat" entry, +0.5.
The result (+0.7, -0.4, +0.5) is exactly row 1 of the table. A multiplication that touches every row returns one row, so real models skip the multiplication and read the row directly.

Multiplying a one-hot vector with 4,096 entries by the 4,096 by 384 table would cost 2 x 4,096 x 384 = 3,145,728 floating-point operations to produce 384 numbers that a lookup copies directly, 1,536 bytes at 4 bytes each.
steps.heading: At the story model's scale the lookup is a memory read, not arithmetic
